headline: 電影劇場三新作
context: 英國藝文圈本週有三部新作登場。動畫片《The Pout-Pout Fish》由尼克・奧佛曼（Nick Offerman）配音，劇評認為故事平淡，配音是全片唯一亮點。愛丁堡藝穗新戲《QFWFQ》改編自卡爾維諾（Italo Calvino）小說《如果在冬夜，一個旅人》，以後設手法呈現原著的超現實敘事。改編自1973年小說的奇幻片《Momo and the Time Thieves》，講述灰衣人誘騙世人把時間存進銀行、換取世人不再享受當下的寓言故事。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Offerman leads a talented cast, but this preschool picture book spinoff fails to inspire Grumpy Mr Fish (Nick Offerman) has a reputation for being a sourpuss, but when he teams up with baby sea dragon Pip (Nina Oyama) to locate a wish-granting fish, it’s pretty much guaranteed that we will discover some sort of heart of gold lurking beneath his gloomy exterior. Not that a picture book for the two to four-year-old crowd can’t be expanded into a satisfying narrative feature film universe, but this high seas adventure as personal growth is fairly by-the-numbers stuff. Based on the books by Deborah Diesen and Dan Hanna, The Pout-Pout Fish’s animation lacks the charm of the books’ illustrations, and the writing is uninspired. Sample exposition-dump: “Did you not hear what they just said? Someone else is looking for Shimmer! And they’ve got a head start! If they get to her first, she won’t have any wish power left!” When the script tries to be more distinctive, you kind of wish they hadn’t bothered – a trio of pink dolphins reference lip-fillers and parody Mean Girls in a way that will be utterly meaningless to the tots at whom the film is aimed, while not being clever enough for their parents. Even the fact that the dolphins are voiced by Amy Sedaris doesn’t help much. So is there anything to like ? The lead character’s vocal stylings are a high point, because Offerman does have one of the great voices. (His entertaining autobiography Paddle Your Own Canoe is well worth the audiobook version.) The man’s voice – an exquisite walnut burr, burnished to a deep amber lustre – can almost, though not quite, elevate bland fare like this uninspiring effort. It’s pretty much the only reason to watch, or at the very least, listen. Continue reading...
sources.title: The Pout-Pout Fish review – Nick Offerman is best thing in kids cartoon adventure on the high seas

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Summerhall, Edinburgh Gregory Nussen spins Italo Calvino’s surrealist authorial intrusions into a fascinating, playful and political show How to adapt an unadaptable novel famed for its postmodern surrealism and authorial intrusions? For Los Angeles performer Gregory Nussen, there can be only one solution: a play built out of postmodern surrealism and authorial intrusions. That is what becomes of Italo Calvino’s If on a Winter’s Night a Traveller as filtered, refracted and reinvented by Nussen and directed by Hannah Pilkes. What in 1979 was a head-spinning novel about the reader trying to make sense of the novel’s unrelated manuscripts becomes, with the actor’s charm, wit and storytelling chops, a playful one-person show that has a fierce political heart beneath its metatheatrical games. At Summerhall, Edinburgh , until 31 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...
sources.title: QFWFQ review – If On a Winter’s Night a Traveller is taken in a bold new direction

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This new adaptation of Michael Ende’s 1973 novel contains some neat parables for our digitally nihilistic age, but even a mystical tortoise can’t save it it from monotony Momo – the 1973 fantasy novel by German author Michael Ende, who also wrote The Neverending Story – has been adapted in live and animated forms before, in 1986 and 2001. This latest version, too, is ostensibly a live-action film – but it’s been made with so many visual effects it might as well have been a cartoon. Still, the residual human element represented by the cast feels necessary, given the story is about the dangers of letting capitalism suck away our ability to enjoy the moment. Over the years, readers have posited all kinds of metaphorical interpretations of the plot, which involves a world where grey beings arrive and con everyone into literally “banking” their time, so as to have it all to themselves. Only the urchin Momo, here played by teen actor Alexa Goodall (whose gorgeous supernova of ginger curls is practically another character in the film), can save the world. Continue reading...
sources.title: Momo and the Time Thieves review – kids’ fantasy jaunt sticks the boot into capitalism

thread_text:
英國藝文圈本週有三部新作登場。

動畫片《The Pout-Pout Fish》由尼克・奧佛曼（Nick Offerman）配音，劇評認為故事平淡，配音是全片唯一亮點。愛丁堡藝穗新戲《QFWFQ》改編自卡爾維諾（Italo Calvino）小說《如果在冬夜，一個旅人》，以後設手法呈現原著的超現實敘事。改編自1973年小說的奇幻片《Momo and the Time Thieves》，講述灰衣人誘騙世人把時間存進銀行、換取世人不再享受當下的寓言故事。
